title: Crossbuck and Nothing Else
hook: No gates. No bells. No lights.
scene: A yellow round sign with an X on it, and then two hundred feet on, a white crossbuck and two rails through the gravel. That's the whole crossing. No arms, no bells, nothing that will tell you. The corn is high enough on the left that you cannot see up the line, and a train doing fifty is quieter than people expect until it isn't.

source.psdp_skill: Skill twelve: driving on rural roads
source.teaching_target: PSDP twelve Railroad crossings + DOL 4.7 parent (not Light rail).

decision: An unmarked crossing, and you can't see up the line.

options.text: Slow, roll down the window, look both ways and listen, then cross
options.result: You come down to almost nothing, drop the glass, look left and right and left again, and hear nothing. Then you cross without stopping on the rails.

options.text: No gates means no active line — keep your speed
options.result: The gates are missing because nobody built any. The line is live. Absence of arms is not absence of trains.

options.text: Stop on the rails to get a better look both ways
options.result: You park the Menace on the one strip of ground you must never stop on. The rails are not a viewpoint.

options.text: Speed up to be across sooner
options.result: You take a blind crossing at speed on gravel. Less time exposed, no time to react.

debrief: At a crossing with no gates or lights: slow down, look both ways, listen, and be ready to stop.
